events.title: Thomas Cromwell executed; Henry VIII weds Catherine Howard
events.description: On the same day, Henry VIII's powerful chief minister Thomas Cromwell was beheaded after being condemned without a trial under a bill of attainder. Henry also married his fifth wife, Catherine Howard.
events.significance: Cromwell had driven the English Reformation and the break with Rome. His fall showed how quickly favor could vanish at the Tudor court.

events.title: Robespierre sent to the guillotine
events.description: Maximilien Robespierre and his ally Louis Antoine de Saint-Just were executed in Paris. Both had been leading figures of the Reign of Terror.
events.significance: Their deaths ended the Terror and shifted the French Revolution toward a less radical phase.

events.title: Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia
events.description: A month after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, Austria-Hungary formally declared war on the Kingdom of Serbia. The declaration came at the end of the July Crisis.
events.significance: Alliances pulled the great powers in one after another, and the conflict grew into World War I.

events.title: United States begins occupation of Haiti
events.description: U.S. forces began an occupation of Haiti that lasted 19 years.
events.significance: The occupation shaped Haiti's politics and finances for a generation. It remains a prominent example of early 20th-century American intervention in the Caribbean.
